title: How to merge PDFs without losing quality
excerpt: A practical merge workflow: choose file order, preserve page content and check the downloaded PDF before sharing.
author: The MY PDF FIX Team
body:
## What merging preserves — and what to check

A PDF can contain selectable text, vector drawings, scanned images and interactive features. MY PDF FIX's [Merge PDF](/merge-pdf) copies pages with pdf-lib in your browser; it does not deliberately render every page as an image. This avoids the resolution loss that comes from a rasterized copy. It does not mean the output is byte-for-byte identical to its inputs: PDF objects are rewritten, and the document has a new structure.

Keep the source files. Page appearance and text are only part of the document. Bookmarks, attachments, form behavior, links and digital signatures need separate checks. A rewritten PDF should not be treated as the original signed document.

## Example: put an appendix after a report

Suppose you have a three-page report and a two-page appendix. This example describes the expected page order, rather than a measured result for your files.

1. Open [Merge PDF](/merge-pdf) and add the report first, then the appendix.
2. Check the displayed list. If a file is misplaced, remove it and add it again to put it at the end. There is no drag-to-sort file control.
3. Click **Process**, then **Download**.
4. Open the saved PDF. It should have five pages: the report on pages 1–3 and the appendix on pages 4–5.

If you need to change individual page positions afterward, use [Reorder Pages](/reorder-pdf-pages). That tool requires every page exactly once; it cannot omit or duplicate pages.

## Check the downloaded file, not just the success message

Inspect a page with small text and one with images. Zoom in and compare them with the originals. Try selecting a sentence that was selectable before merging. Search for a known phrase. Check the boundary between the files so that no page is missing or repeated, and test any important links or filled fields.

A scanned page remains an image; merging does not add searchable text or OCR. If a source scan is sideways, [rotate that file](/rotate-pdf) before merging. Rotation applies to every page in the selected file.

## File size and privacy limits

Output size depends on the source resources and PDF serialization; there is no fixed ratio to the sum of the inputs. [Compress PDF](/compress-pdf) can try to reduce a large result, but Recommended and Strong may rasterize pages and remove selectable text. Use Light when avoiding rasterization matters, and compare the output.

The document processing does not upload your PDF contents. Loading the website and Google verification can still make network requests, while optional tracking follows your privacy choices. Read the [Privacy Policy](/privacy) for that distinction. Large documents can exceed browser memory, so reduce the batch size if merging fails.
